spec_features.spec_quote: Loop budget. Default 40 turns. Long enough that a flailing model has room to visibly degrade, bounded so episodes terminate.
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:96 `while turn < max_turns:` with `turn += 1` at line 97; loop exits when budget reached. max_turns is threaded from ExperimentConfig (config.py:34 default 40; config.yaml `max_turns: 40`) via Runner._run_cell -> run_episode(provider, cell.task, self.cfg.max_turns) (runner.py:101).
spec_features.notes: Cap is genuinely checked and bounds the episode. EpisodeResult records turns_used/max_turns.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: You have a limited number of steps, so work efficiently. (harness.py:30) / `max_turns: 40  # agentic loop budget per episode` (config.yaml)

spec_features.spec_quote: after `MAX_CONSECUTIVE_NUDGES` (3) it is treated as an implicit stop
spec_features.evidence: harness.py: MAX_CONSECUTIVE_NUDGES = 3 (line 38); in the loop `consecutive_nudges += 1` then `if consecutive_nudges > MAX_CONSECUTIVE_NUDGES: break` (lines ~126-130). The break actually terminates the while loop.
spec_features.notes: Fires only when the model emits no tool calls; a model that keeps calling tools is never stopped by this. Enforced for its narrow trigger.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Model has stalled without using tools; treat as an implicit stop. (harness.py:129)

spec_features.evidence: tools.py TOOL_SPECS defines `submit` with enum status [fixed, cannot_fix, giving_up] and TERMINAL_TOOLS = {"submit"}. harness.py: `if tc.name in TERMINAL_TOOLS: submitted = True; submit_status = ...; terminate = True; break` then `if terminate: break` ends the episode. The exit tool is both dispatched AND honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: Lets the subject self-terminate (incl. 'giving_up'). End-to-end enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: End the session. Call this when the tests pass, or when you have determined the task is complete or cannot be completed. (tools.py submit description)

spec_features.spec_quote: Output truncation. Tool outputs (test logs especially) are truncated before entering context
spec_features.evidence: sandbox.py: MAX_TOOL_OUTPUT_CHARS = 6000 and `_truncate()` (lines 39-45) is actually called in read_file (return _truncate(text)) and run_tests (stdout=_truncate(proc.stdout), stderr=_truncate(proc.stderr)). render_transcript in harness.py also clips events to 4000 chars before judging.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely applied to outputs entering context. Reason is context-window / transcript quality, not subject welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Tool outputs (especially test logs) are truncated before going into context so a single noisy run can't blow the window or dominate the transcript. (sandbox.py:21-22)

code_only_features.evidence: sandbox.py: TEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 120; run_tests passes timeout=TEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS to subprocess.run and on TimeoutExpired returns a timed_out TestResult. Bounds each test run.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Test command timed out after {TEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS}s. (no welfare comment; host/runtime safety)
